svg.title: Figure 4. Wire by neuropil
svg.desc: Figure 4. Twelve rows, one per neuropil. Bars of the share of all wire that ends in each: GNG 10.1%, ANm 5.8%, AVLP(R) 4.1%, LegNp(T2)(R) 4.0%, LegNp(T3)(R) 3.9%, LegNp(T2)(L) 3.9%, AVLP(L) 3.8%, LegNp(T1)(L) 3.4%, LegNp(T3)(L) 3.3%, SAD 3.3%, LegNp(T1)(R) 3.1%, PB 2.9%. Beside each, a dot for the summed length of its internal connections divided by the mean of 1000 permutations of its own cell types: GNG 0.809, ANm 0.729, AVLP(R) 0.863, LegNp(T2)(R) 0.885, LegNp(T3)(R) 0.894, LegNp(T2)(L) 0.895, AVLP(L) 0.879, LegNp(T1)(L) 0.891, LegNp(T3)(L) 0.922, SAD 0.682, LegNp(T1)(R) 0.885, PB 0.767. 89 of 105 neuropil surfaces hold cell types and 6.6% of the wire stays inside one of them. All 48 neuropils large enough to test sit below their permuted mean, 41 of them below every permutation, and AL(L) comes closest at 0.974.
